doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Faith and music
summary: He belongs to no religion but credits God for his ability and tries to be a good person.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well last sort of question — you seem like a man of faith and over the years has the profession of music challenged your faith sort of like the disconnect between the two? Maybe even going back to when you were a kid? © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

I don’t know. I have faith in what I believe in you know. I don’t understand a lot of things and so I don’t join any religions or anything like that. Because I don’t understand it. And what I do understand is most religions don’t make sense to me you know. So all I know is what I call God and what God has done for me you know. And that’s — the faith that I have is that I got it from God, I know it’s from God or whatever you want to call God. Whatever it is gave me this talent, this ability to do like I do. And maybe some day I’ll figure it out but I haven’t figured it out yet. And until then I just believe that I should be a good person and not treat anybody bad and not boast about anything that I’ve done because I know it’s not me, it’s a natural ability that I have that is from God, what I call God.
